claim: The Amazon Route 53 features page sums up the routing choices: latency based routing sends users to the AWS Region with the lowest possible latency, Geo DNS sends users to an endpoint you specify by geographic location, geoproximity routing sends traffic to the geographically nearest resource and helps apply data residency preferences, and IP-based routing uses the CIDR block of the query-originating IP address.
question: Which routing policy fits lowest latency, user geography, nearest resource with data residency, or client CIDR blocks?

values.display: the AWS region that provides the lowest possible latency
based on the end user’s geographic location

evidence.quote: Route end users to the AWS region that provides the lowest possible latency.
Route end users to a particular endpoint that you specify based on the end user’s geographic location.
Improves application responsiveness for your end users and helps apply data residency preferences by routing traffic to the geographically nearest resource.
Fine-tune your DNS routing approach based on the Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) block that the query-originating IP address belongs to.

claim: The Amazon Route 53 features page describes Traffic Flow as global traffic management that routes users to the best endpoint based on geoproximity, latency, health and other considerations, DNS failover as automatic rerouting of visitors to an alternate location to avoid site outages, and private DNS for Amazon VPC as managing custom domain names for internal AWS resources without exposing DNS data to the public internet.
question: Which Route 53 feature manages internal names without exposing DNS data, and which one reroutes visitors to avoid outages?

values.display: route end users to the best endpoint for your application
Automatically route your website visitors to an alternate location to avoid site outages.
without exposing DNS data to the public Internet

evidence.quote: Easy-to-use and cost-effective global traffic management: route end users to the best endpoint for your application based on geoproximity, latency, health, and other considerations.
Automatically route your website visitors to an alternate location to avoid site outages.
Manage custom domain names for your internal AWS resources without exposing DNS data to the public Internet.
